purpose: Ensure a published case report can be reconstructed from its immutable answer snapshot, evidence, legal sources, citations, privacy state and verification history.
core_principle: REPORT → SNAPSHOT → EVIDENCE → LAW → CITATIONS → QUALITY GATE → VERIFICATION HISTORY
rules: A historical report must be reconstructed from its historical snapshot references, not from today's answer.
Current source changes must not rewrite the contents of a historical snapshot.
A report is reproducible only if material dependencies can be identified and their recorded versions/scopes are preserved.
A missing external source does not justify inventing its former content.
Where a source can no longer be retrieved, the report may remain historically recorded but reproducibility must disclose the limitation.
Material revisions create a new snapshot and preserve the predecessor.
hard_stops: Never reconstruct a historical report by silently substituting current law.
Never substitute new evidence into an old snapshot.
Never mark a report reproducible when a material dependency is missing.
Never alter the historical report to make reconstruction appear complete.
Never expose restricted evidence merely to satisfy reproducibility.
